data.title: Tosca's 2026 Sustainability Report Makes the Case for Packaging as Critical Supply Chain Infrastructure
data.description:
BRUSSELS, BE / ACCESS Newswire / November 20, 2026 / Tosca, a global leader in reusable packaging and pooling solutions, has released its 2026 Sustainability Report, calling for a shift in how businesses evaluate transport packaging: from a purchased commodity to a strategic component of supply chain infrastructure.

As food supply chains become more automated and face mounting cost and regulatory pressures, packaging decisions increasingly influence operational performance. The report examines how reusable packaging can reduce food loss, labor requirements and transportation inefficiencies while documenting Tosca's progress toward its global sustainability goals.

"Companies invest significant resources in optimizing equipment, labor and transportation, yet packaging is still too often evaluated primarily on unit price," said Eric Frank, CEO of Tosca. "That approach overlooks its role in keeping automated lines running, protecting products and moving goods efficiently. Packaging is an operational input and should be evaluated with the same discipline as the infrastructure around it."

Measuring the Impact Beyond Packaging Waste

The report highlights how reusable packaging and pooling systems deliver measurable benefits across customer operations. For example,

  • Less product damage and food waste: Strong, rigid crates protect products during handling and transport, reducing damage to fresh produce by an average of 6-9%. For eggs, Tosca's reusable packaging reduces damage by more than 50%.
  • Lower labor requirements: Retail-ready reusable packaging saves 307 labor hours per 100,000 crates compared to corrugated packaging.
  • More efficient transportation: Improved load utilization and fewer journeys can reduce transportation costs by up to 25%, alongside associated emission reductions.
  • Less single-use packaging waste: Tosca's reusable packaging solutions have removed 2.229 million metric tons of corrugated packaging from supply chains, eliminating the associated recycling and disposal requirements.

Advancing Global Sustainability Goals

Tosca reported solid progress in reducing the environmental footprint of its own operations:

  • 30% reduction in global Scope 1 and 2 GHG emissions intensity per operating hour since 2021.
  • 46% of global electricity sourced from renewables in 2025, up from 33% in 2022.
  • 41% reduction in total waste generated compared with 2024.

The report also highlights Tosca's investments in circular infrastructure, including the CP 1208 Circular Pallet, developed from 100% recycled plastic, and expanded RFID-enabled asset tracking to improve supply chain visibility.

Following its first Double Materiality Assessment and formal climate risk assessment in 2025, Tosca updated its sustainability strategy through 2030, targeting 42% reductions in absolute Scope 1 and 2 emissions and Scope 3 emissions against their respective baselines.

"Reducing the footprint of a packaging material is only part of the equation," said Karin Witton, Ph.D., Global Head of Sustainability at Tosca. "We also have to account for the food lost, transportation required and resources consumed throughout the supply chain. Measuring these impacts together helps businesses identify where the greatest environmental and operational improvements can be made."

Download Tosca's 2026 Sustainability Report

About Tosca

Tosca is a global leader in reusable plastic packaging and pooling solutions, helping businesses eliminate waste and improve supply chain performance. Through its reusable containers, pallets, bulk packaging, and end-to-end pooling services, Tosca helps customers protect products, improve operational efficiency, and reduce environmental impact. Serving customers across more than 60 countries, Tosca is committed to advancing circular supply chains and eliminating waste at every turn.

For more information, visit www.toscaltd.com.

data.title: FRO – Third Quarter and Nine Months 2026 Results
data.description:
FRONTLINE PLC REPORTS RESULTS FOR THE THIRD QUARTER ENDED SEPTEMBER 30, 2026

Frontline plc (the “Company”, “Frontline”, “we,” “us,” or “our”), today reported unaudited results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026:

Highlights

  • Profit of $641.4 million, or $2.88 per share for the third quarter of 2026 and adjusted profit1 of $530.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, or $2.38 per share.
  • Declared a cash dividend of $2.38 per share for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Reported revenues of $921.3 million for the third quarter of 2026.
  • Achieved average daily spot time charter equivalent earnings ("TCEs")2 for VLCCs, Suezmax tankers and LR2/Aframax tankers in the third quarter of 2026 of $148,500, $102,500 and $67,800 per day, respectively.
  • Sold two VLCCs built in 2017 for a total sales price of $270.0 million. The transactions generated net cash proceeds of $179.0 million, which were returned to the shareholders through the payment of a special one-time dividend of $0.80 per share in September 2026.
  • Entered into a three-year time charter-out agreement for one Suezmax tanker, built in 2016, at a rate of $80,000 per day, which commenced in October 2026.
  • Entered into a new senior secured revolving reducing credit facility in an amount of up to $731.8 million in November 2026 to refinance the $1,286.0 million secured revolving reducing credit facility, further reducing the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

Lars H. Barstad, Chief Executive Officer of Frontline Management AS, commented:

“The third quarter of 2026 was defined by the escalation in the Middle East, logistical challenges and time-consuming trading patterns. Utilization has since reached extraordinary levels, and freight rates have moved to all-time highs, with asset values following and the entire tanker complex benefiting. As we are well into the fourth quarter of the year, our bookings so far are at the highest levels we have ever recorded across all three of our segments. With the majority of our spot days already fixed, Frontline is positioned to deliver its strongest result ever, both for the fourth quarter and for the full year 2026. The nine months that have passed in 2026 is likely to change the oil trading patterns considerably in the future, making us optimistic for Frontline’s earnings capacity in the years to come.”

Inger M. Klemp, Chief Financial Officer of Frontline Management AS, added:

“From June to November 2026 we reduced our financing costs through a combination of margin reductions on existing facilities for their remaining tenors and full refinancing of selected facilities, contributing to a reduction in the Company’s weighted average interest rate margin of 60 bps from 178 bps at the end of the first quarter of 2026 to 118 bps as of the date of this report.

We believe that the refinancing of, and amendments to, our existing debt facilities have been achieved on highly attractive terms, further strengthening our liquidity position while reducing our borrowing costs and cash breakeven rates. We continue to focus on maintaining our competitive cost structure, breakeven levels and solid balance sheet to ensure that we are well positioned to generate significant cash flow and create value for our shareholders.”

data.title: Evonik CEO Says BASF Ending Takeover Pursuit Removes Source of Uncertainty
data.description:
By Adria Calatayud

Evonik Industries' interim Chief Executive Officer Claus Rettig said BASF's decision to abandon efforts to take over the German chemicals company removes a source of uncertainty for its employees.

"Our plan for the coming years is set. Now we can focus our full energy on Evonik's standalone development," Rettig said. "For our employees, this removes a source of uncertainty."

BASF said Thursday that it would end its pursuit of Evonik after two all-cash offers were rebuffed.

"We are convinced that BASF's derisked all-cash offer of 24 euros per share would have represented significant additional value for Evonik shareholders," BASF Chief Executive  Markus Kamieth said.

The bid valued Evonik at 11.18 billion euros ($12.26 billion), based on share-count data provided by FactSet.

data.title: LEPAS L8, L6 and L4 Earn Five-Star Ratings in 2026 Euro NCAP Assessment
data.description:
WUHU, China, Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- LEPAS, Chery Auto’s Premium NEV brand, has secured five-star safety ratings for its L8, L6 and L4 models under the 2026 assessment protocols. The ratings were announced by the European New Car Assessment Programme (Euro NCAP) on November 18, 2026, as part of its latest assessment covering 10 models across four key areas: Safe Driving, Crash Avoidance, Crash Protection and Post Crash Safety.


The 2026 protocols mark Euro NCAP's most significant update since 2009, introducing more demanding assessments across four areas of vehicle safety. The revised tests place greater emphasis on real-world scenarios, including complex junctions, cyclist dooring and post-crash rescue. In this round, the LEPAS L4 scored 84% in Crash Avoidance, while both the L6 and L8 achieved 87% in Crash Protection and 95% in Post Crash Safety.


The three five-star ratings highlight Chery Auto's extensive experience in vehicle safety development and validation, backed by more than 1,500 crash tests annually across over 67 scenarios. Leveraging Chery Group's "1+7+N" global R&D network, LEPAS brings this expertise to the intelligent LEX Platform. The platform integrates multiple layers of protection covering vehicle structure, occupant safety, battery safety and emergency response, complemented by redundant active safety systems and 360-degree battery protection.

About LEPAS

LEPAS is Chery Auto's Premium NEV brand, dedicated to creating elegant mobility experiences for users worldwide. Committed to becoming the Preferred Brand for Elegant Mobility Life, LEPAS brings together Leopard Aesthetics, Elegant Technology, and Exquisite Space - transforming elegance into a driving experience you can see, feel, and trust. Supported by a growing global dealer network of more than 500 sales and service outlets, LEPAS is expanding its international footprint through localized operations, delivering products and experiences tailored to users across global markets.

About Chery Auto

Founded in 1997, Chery Auto is a global automotive manufacturer specializing in vehicle development, intelligent technologies, and new energy solutions. The company operates in more than 130 countries and regions, supported by a strong international network of research, production, and strategic partnerships. Chery Auto has remained China’s No. 1 passenger vehicle exporter among Chinese brands for 23 consecutive years. Guided by its global philosophy of "In somewhere, For somewhere, Be somewhere," Chery Auto is committed to advancing sustainable mobility through continuous innovation and global collaboration.

data.title: BioVersys reports results from Phase 2a ENABLE study for tuberculosis treatments containing AlpE
data.description:
BioVersys reports results from Phase 2a ENABLE study for tuberculosis treatments containing AlpE

BioVersys reports results from Phase 2a ENABLE study for tuberculosis treatments containing AlpE

PR Newswire

BASEL, Switzerland, Nov. 20, 2026
  • Phase 2a ENABLE study showed early bactericidal activity in all regimens evaluated over 14 days in patients with newly diagnosed drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis
  • AlpE combined with RZE achieved early bactericidal activity comparable to standard-of-care HRZE over 14 days
  • Findings support continued evaluation of AlpE-containing regimens

BASEL, Switzerland, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BioVersys AG (SIX: BIOV), a multi-asset, clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focusing on research and development of novel antibacterial products for serious life-threatening infections caused by multi-drug resistant (MDR) bacteria, announced today results from the completed 14-day Phase 2a ENABLE study of alpibectir in combination with ethionamide (AlpE) in patients with newly diagnosed drug-sensitive pulmonary tuberculosis.

AlpE combines alpibectir with the anti-tuberculosis drug ethionamide and is being advanced through a collaboration between GSK and BioVersys for pulmonary TB and TB meningitis.

The phase 2a ENABLE study (NCT06748937) evaluated a 45 mg dose of alpibectir, higher than previously studied, in combination with 125mg or 250mg of ethionamide. AlpE was evaluated alone and in combination with rifampicin, pyrazinamide and ethambutol (RZE), replacing isoniazid in the standard-of-care HRZE regimen. The ENABLE study is conducted by TASK as part of the European Union Innovative Health Initiative Joint Undertaking (EU IHI JU) project UNITE4TB.

All regimens displayed bactericidal activity. Early bactericidal activity was ethionamide dose-dependent, with the regimen containing 250 mg ethionamide more active than the regimen containing 125 mg ethionamide. Although not designed for formal comparison between treatment arms, the AlpE 45 mg/250 mg-RZE regimen demonstrated EBA results that were numerically similar to standard-of-care HRZE, indicating that AlpE could potentially replace isoniazid in the treatment of isoniazid-resistant TB. AlpE was generally well tolerated and showed an acceptable safety profile over 14 days in this trial. 

Dr. David Barros-Aguirre, Head of Global Health Medicines R&D, GSK, and UNITE4TB Project Lead, said: "These early findings add to the growing clinical data for AlpE and support its continued evaluation as part of potential future TB regimens that could be simpler and more effective than those available today. By combining GSK's science and innovation with the expertise of BioVersys and partners across UNITE4TB, we're aiming to improve treatment options for people affected by TB."

Dr. Marc Gitzinger, Chief Executive Officer, BioVersys, said: "The results from the Phase 2a ENABLE trial provide important clinical evidence supporting the continued development of AlpE as a potential component of future tuberculosis treatment regimens. Invaluable contributions from patients, investigators and partners made this study possible. We look forward to building on these results through the ongoing clinical programme and our continued collaboration with GSK. AlpE originated from a collaboration with Pasteur Institute Lille, BioVersys and GSK, and represents a formidable example of successful private-public partnerships to advance this important innovation into the space of global health. We are also grateful to the public funding agencies supporting this program such as EU IMI, EDCTP and others."

Dr. Michel Pieren, Clinical Program Team Leader, BioVersys, said: "The clinical microbiology data presented at the Union Conference further strengthen our understanding of how alpibectir potentiates the activity of ethionamide and its active metabolite. These findings provide additional support for the mechanism underlying the clinical activity observed with AlpE and help inform the continued development of alpibectir-containing treatment regimens."

The results were presented at the Union World Conference on Lung Health, taking place from 17 to 20 November 2026 in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. The conference programme included presentations covering the ENABLE efficacy, safety and pharmacokinetic findings, the further development of AlpE-containing regimens, and clinical data from an earlier Phase 2a study.

A separate clinical trial, STEP2C, conducted through UNITE4TB, with GSK and BioVersys supporting the clinical development of AlpE is currently evaluating the activity of AlpE-RZE during the first two months of treatment. This Phase 2b trial (NCT05807399) reported first-patient-first-visit in March 2026 and is conducted in six African countries under the European Union's IMI2 UNITE4TB project, with the Institute of Infectious Diseases and Tropical Medicine, LMU University Hospital Munich as the trial sponsor. A separate Phase 2 programme is advancing in TB meningitis, led by BioVersys.

About BioVersys
BioVersys AG is a multi-asset, clinical stage biopharmaceutical company focused on identifying, developing and commercializing novel antibacterial products for serious life-threatening infections caused by multi-drug resistant ("MDR") bacteria. Derived from the company's two internal technology platforms (TRIC and Ansamycin Chemistry), candidates are designed and developed to overcome resistance mechanisms, block virulence production and directly affect the pathogenesis of harmful bacteria towards the identification of new treatment options in the antimicrobial and microbiome fields. This enables BioVersys to address the high unmet medical need for new treatments against life-threatening resistant bacterial infections and bacteria-exacerbated chronic inflammatory microbiome disorders. The company's most advanced research and development programs address nosocomial infections of Acinetobacter baumannii (BV100, Phase 3), and tuberculosis (alpibectir, Phase 2, in collaboration with GlaxoSmithKline (GSK) and a consortium of the University of Lille, France). BioVersys is located in the biotech hub of Basel, Switzerland.

About Alpibectir
Alpibectir (previously known as BVL-GSK098) is a small molecule developed from BioVersys' award winning Transcriptional Regulatory Inhibitory Compounds (TRIC) platform in a successful collaboration with GSK, the Institut Pasteur Lille and the University of Lille. Alpibectir acts through a novel mode of action, potentiating the activity of the anti-TB drug ethionamide (Eto). Alpibectir is being studied for its potential to lower the efficacious human dose of Eto, minimizing of dose-dependent side effects, and overcome Eto resistance. The combination alpibectir/Eto (AlpE) is being developed for the treatment of pulmonary TB and TB meningitis. In 2023 AlpE was granted orphan-drug designation (ODD) for the treatment of tuberculosis, by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (U.S. FDA) providing for certain incentives including seven years US market exclusivity. Similarly in 2025, AlpE was granted Orphan Designation from the European Medicines Agency (EMA), providing for certain incentives including 10-year EU market exclusivity.

About UNITE4TB
UNITE4TB is one of nine projects within the AMR Accelerator. Working across a global clinical trials network, UNITE4TB conducts regulatory standard Phase 2 clinical trials to accelerate clinical evaluation of novel drugs and combinations of drugs for tuberculosis (TB). Innovative adaptive trial designs, treatment response biomarkers, pharmacokinetic-pharmacodynamic models and Artificial Intelligence / Deep Learning techniques are integrated across study protocols, deploying cutting-edge methodologies to find antibiotic regimens with the highest likelihood of improved clinical efficacy.

This project has received funding from the Innovative Medicines Initiative 2 Joint Undertaking (JU) under grant agreement No 101007873. (DZIF), and Ludwig-Maximilians-Universität München (LMU). EFPIA/AP contribute 50% of funding, whereas the contribution of DZIF and the LMU University Hospital Munich has been granted by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research.

Consumer prices excluding fresh food climbed 2.2% in October from a year earlier, reinforcing expectations for another interest-rate increase by the central bank.

China's AI Firms Are Addicted to Nvidia Chips. Now They Are Facing Withdrawal.

The move by the U.S. to cut off Chinese access to high-end computing power has dealt a blow to Beijing's artificial-intelligence ambitions.

The Claude chatbot maker's backers invested capital at an unprecedented scale into the artificial-intelligence giant in a departure from venture's usual playbook.

The bipartisan effort to streamline federal permitting split Democrats over environmental concerns.

U.S. Jobless Claims Unexpectedly Move Higher

Canada Producer Prices Rise Again in October, Buoyed by Energy Products

Statistics Canada's industrial product price index increased 0.3% in October from the month before, a softer advance than the downwardly revised 1.5% increase in September.

South African Reserve Bank Maintains Main Repo Rate at 7.25%

SARB Governor Lesetja Kganyago said South Africa's inflation has been much higher than expected and fixed investment is too low.

data.title: ADDEX THERAPEUTICS TO REPORT  2026 THIRD QUARTER FINANCIAL RESULTS  AND HOST CONFERENCE CALL ON NOVEMBER 25, 2026
data.description:
Geneva, Switzerland, November 20, 2026 - Addex Therapeutics (SIX and Nasdaq: ADXN), a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders, today announced that it will report its 2026 Third Quarter Financial Results on November 25, 2026. Tim Dyer, CEO, will provide a business update and review of the Addex product pipeline during a teleconference and webcast for investors, analysts and media at 16:00 CET (15:00 GMT / 10:00 EDT / 07:00 PDT) on November 25, 2026.

Title:  Addex Therapeutics Reports 2026 Third Quarter financial results and Provides Corporate Update
Date: November 25, 2026
Time: 16:00 CET (15:00 BST / 10:00 EST / 07:00 PST)

Joining the Conference Call:

  1. Participants are required to register in advance of the conference using the link provided below. Upon registering, each participant will be provided with Participant Dial-in numbers, and a unique Personal PIN.

  2. In the 10 minutes prior to the call start time, participants will need to use the conference access information provided in the e-mail received at the point of registering. Participants may also use the call me feature instead of dialing the nearest dial in number.

Webcast registration link: Registration webcast

Conference call registration link: Registration conference media

About Addex Therapeutics

Addex Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing a portfolio of novel small molecule allosteric modulators for neurological disorders. Addex's lead drug candidate, dipraglurant (mGlu5 negative allosteric modulator or NAM), is under evaluation for future development in brain injury recovery, including post-stroke and traumatic brain injury recovery. Addex has selected a GABAB PAM drug candidate for development in substance use disorders and has successfully completed IND enabling studies. In addition, Addex  is advancing a differentiated GABAB PAM compound for the treatment of chronic cough. Addex holds an 8.5% equity interest in a private spin out company, Neurosterix US Holdings LLC, which is advancing a portfolio of allosteric modulator programs, including M4 PAM for schizophrenia, psychosis and mood-related disorders and mGlu7 NAM for mood disorders. Addex has also invested in Stalicla, a private Swiss company pioneering a precision medicine approach for neurodevelopmental and neuropsychiatric disorders.

Addex shares are listed on the SIX Swiss Exchange and American Depositary Shares representing its shares are listed on the NASDAQ Capital Market, and trade under the ticker symbol “ADXN” on each exchange. For more information, visit www.addextherapeutics.com.
